method: Three independent judges (physicist-founder, deep-tech investor, Thiel-fellow operator) read the red-teamed dossiers without seeing each other; all three picked the same BEST BET, FASTEST PROOF and MOONSHOT. Judge files: research/stage3/judge_{physicist,investor,operator}.json.

BEST_BET.why: ~10x lower energy per bit delivered than HBM (0.37 vs 3.95 pJ/b) survived every correction because it comes from geometry (no PHY/interposer/TSV path), not heroic cell physics; 1 bit/cell, 16 tiers; refresh-light (~225x rarer than Si at 105-125 C); ~90 W/GPU saved in the planning case (48-169 W).
BEST_BET.decisive_experiment: Gate A+ by month 11 (~$240k standalone): 2T0C oxide coupons (IGZO / In-poor IGZO / IGO / Ga-free ZTO), single vs series write gate, -0.5 vs -0.7 V hold, after a real D2O-labelled fusion bond; >=1e5 cells per split measured for drift, cross-temperature, RTN and the directly measured 1e-4 retention quantile.
BEST_BET.kill: Kill the capacity claim at M11 if every split fails 1e-4-tail retention >=1 s at 105 C, drift sigma <=75 mV, or RTN 1e-4 quantile <=100 mV.

FASTEST_PROOF.why: No fab, no new physics: ~$124k on DRAM Bender + open DDR5 testers gives a binary by month 6 and the error budget every cell concept relies on (~9x refresh-energy cut on DDR5 RDIMMs at 85 C with chipkill kept; ~13x on retired DDR4 behind CXL).
FASTEST_PROOF.kill: NO-GO if the chipkill-safe interval incl. VRT is <4x the JEDEC window at 65 C, multi-chip events >10%, or the 1 h grade holds on <95% of modules over 1,000 h.

MOONSHOT.why: Highest remaining ceiling: 64 tiers x 2 b = 5.9x 1-beta density, ~2.3x bits/$ vs 2026 (1.1-1.4x vs projected 2032), ~25x lower refresh power, no EUV; the single-film closure was killed, the two-film notched write pocket needs three never-built process modules (P(closure) ~20%) — a process-integration problem where persistence has many knobs.
MOONSHOT.decisive_experiment: Planar GO #1A at M9 on the shared lot; 2-tier vertical closure coupon GO #1B at M14-16 (~$0.4M standalone to the gate).
MOONSHOT.kill: M18: if the 2-tier coupon has not closed, kill single-etch and fall back to the coaxial per-tier cell.

PORTFOLIO.thesis: One shared Oxide Tail Statistics lot answers the question seven concepts share, so the $1M funds evidence for most of the portfolio at once; the DRAM-error study sets the ECC budget every cell model uses; conditional spends (AND-stack closure coupon, Hot-Side Gate B) release only after gates pass.
PORTFOLIO.facility_first: Purdue Birck Nanotechnology Center (external user), with Georgia Tech IEN as second site
PORTFOLIO.recruit_first: An oxide-semiconductor device-reliability physicist (IGZO-class PBTI/hydrogen/RTN, aA leakage-tail metrology on >=1e4-device arrays, 2T0C experience)

biggest_unknown: The statistical tails of scaled amorphous-oxide transistors (IGZO/IGO/ZTO, <=0.01-0.02 um2) after the full <=400 C hydrogen, thermal and bonding budget at 85-125 C: the 1e-4 to 2e-5 quantile of aA-level off-state leakage and the 1e-4 quantile of ns-to-s RTN.
monday_action: In <=2 hours, write a one-page 'Oxide Tail Spec' (rows: device structures; columns: channel splits, device area, timescale, temperature, H/thermal dose, bond split, pass/kill line per concept) from the dossiers' section 5 and 11 thresholds, and send it to one oxide-FET university group with external-user access (the judges name Purdue Birck) to ask whether they can run it and at what cost.
headline: No free lunch and no physics kill: 10,525 distinct ideas funneled to 10 concepts; all 10 survived 181 red-team objections but were downgraded (~2x on headline claims). The durable step changes are energy per bit moved next to compute (~10x), refresh bought with coding (~9x), and density from tier count without EUV (4.6-5.9x) — not cheap bits (<=1.6x bits/$ vs a projected 2032 incumbent).
